subject: QBR preflight: slot strategy, cache wins, and batching experiments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR preflight: slot strategy, cache wins, and batching experiments

Team —

We’re consolidating the infra section of the QBR pre-read and I want to lock the decisions where possible before Monday’s leadership review. High-level asks below; please see the attached workbook for numbers I pulled together (tabbed by model family and region).

Asks (short):
- Confirm which slot allocation policy we land on for hosted vs. dedicated (priority vs. balanced). I’ve put a proposed split on tab "slot-proposals".
- Finalize the batching experiment baseline we present: show 8/16/32 batch sizes with KV cache enabled vs. disabled.
- Agree a procurement timeline for a potential 4-week GPU burst in Nov (2x V100 -> A100 mix) and whether we need a formal purchase request to CloudBuy.

Quick context: the workbook includes measured changes to utilization and token unit cost from the recent Canary runs (region us-west-2): batching to 32 increased average GPU utilization from ~34% to ~73% for text-generate workloads; enabling prefix KV cache saved ~18% token emissions on average for our cold-start patterns. Those are in the "experiment-summary" tab.

Schedule: I’d like a 30-minute sync today if possible to close the slide-level asks; otherwise please flag any blockers in-thread.

Attachments: qbr-capacity-preflight.xlsx, batching-experiment-summary.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR preflight: slot strategy, cache wins, and batching experiments

Marissa —

Thanks for the preflight. Quick read-through and some data to surface for the slides:

- Batching results (summary):
  * Batch 8 -> average latency 220ms, GPU util ~41%, token unit cost baseline.
  * Batch 16 -> latency 260ms, GPU util ~58%, token unit cost -14% vs batch8.
  * Batch 32 -> latency 410ms (p95 spikes for long sequences), GPU util ~73%, token unit cost -27% vs batch8.

- KV caching:
  * For chat-like traces we saw 18–22% fewer decode tokens in the first 2 sec of sessions with prefix cache enabled (warm paths).
  * Cache benefits are additive with batching; we should show combined numbers (batch 16 + cache = ~35% unit cost reduction on these traces).

- Risk notes for slides:
  * Batch 32 introduces p95 latency regressions for >1k token sequences — need a fallback SLO policy (route long seqs to smaller batch or dedicated slot).
  * Cache invalidation window and memory tax: some model variants increased memory pressure by ~12% with large KV windows.

Recommendation for the QBR decision slide: present two clean options — (A) "Conservative" = batch16 + cache + priority slots for latency-sensitive tenants; (B) "Aggressive" = batch32 + cache + canary long-seq routing + procurement for 4-week burst. Call out expected token-cost delta and 95th latency delta.

I can join a quick sync at 12:30 if that helps. I also dropped a short PDF (batching-experiment-summary.pdf) into the Drive link to make the numbers slide-ready.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik —

Looping in CloudBuy (procurement) so we can get a sanity check on lead times and whether they can support a 4-week burst in November.

Notes for procurement:
- We’re considering an on-prem/marketplace mix: 8x A100 spot-equivalents + 4x reserved V100 for predictable throughput.
- Target start: 2026-11-08; preferred end: 2026-12-06.
- Budget range (rough): $380k–$520k depending on reserved vs. spot split.

CloudBuy — can you confirm what the minimum lead time and contractual steps are for a 4-week commitment at this scale? Also flag any SLA add-ons needed for our dedicated pools.

Marissa: I updated the workbook with a procurement timeline tab and a short checklist (vendor contracts, SOC 2 attestation for the new hosts, KMS key handoff). See the Drive link.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Procurement Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — clear and helpful. A few quick leadership-level decisions so the slides can be finalized: 

1) We will present the two-option approach Karthik proposed (Conservative vs Aggressive). Call out the expected cost delta and p95 latency risk on the slide.
2) Approve the procurement runway for the 4-week burst conditioned on CloudBuy confirming lead time and a final budget within the $380k–$520k range. Olga, if CloudBuy can confirm by EOD Monday, consider this approved and proceed with the purchase request.
3) For the QBR narrative: focus on the operational levers (batching, KV cache, slot routing) and the measurable economics (token cost per request and util uplift). Keep one slide with fallback SLO rules for long sequences.

Marissa, finalize the pre-read with the selected slide deck template and send to execs by EOD Sunday. Karthik — please make sure the "combined numbers" slide includes the p95 impact line for long sequences (we need it called out). Olga — please confirm vendor lead time and loop back.

SGTM.

—Lauren Bishop
